summary: Token exchange failures for console and CLI after device-trust policy schema update (SCIM sync conflict)
description: After a device-trust policy attribute normalization change rolled to production, several internal console and CLI sessions started failing during the token-exchange step. Affected service accounts and users receive a 403 or TokenExchangeError during refresh. Impact: internal tooling (deploys, oncall runbooks) intermittently blocked for engineers with recently synced Okta groups.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Have an Okta user or service account with device_trust attribute set to 'Trusted' pre-change
2) Trigger SCIM delta sync from Okta to Redwood SCIM provisioning service
3) Attempt to authenticate via CLI (redwood login) or access console routes that perform server-side token exchange
4) Observe TokenExchangeError or 403 when the RBAC role mapping lookup runs
logs: 2026-03-10T08:14:22Z auth-service ERROR token-exchange: TokenExchangeError: subject claim missing expected attribute 'device_trust_status' (okta_id=00u12345)
2026-03-10T08:14:23Z scim-provisioner WARN mapping: attribute 'device_trust'->'device_trust_status' normalized as null for 37 updated users
2026-03-10T08:14:25Z rbac-service INFO role-resolver: no groups resolved for okta_id=00u12345, default-role not applied
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: recent policy normalization changed attribute name and SCIM mapping, causing missing claim during token exchange
Checked deployment history: identity team deployed schema normalization v2.1 to scim-provisioner at 2026-03-10T07:50Z (PR #4221)
Confirmed delta syncs after the deploy produced entries with empty device_trust_status for users that previously had 'device_trust' populated
Observed RBAC mapping expects okta claim 'device_trust_status' to construct derived role names; missing claim leads to role-resolve failure and token exchange abort
Edge case: long-lived service tokens that revalidated against AD/Okta were fine until next SCIM delta; newly synced or re-provisioned accounts are affected
comments: 2026-03-10T09:02 - Ravi Singh (assignee): Oncall SRE reproducing locally; collecting audit logs from okta-app provisioning. Pinned scim-provisioner to previous image in staging for comparison.

2026-03-10T09:45 - Asha Patel (identity eng): Confirmed PR #4221 introduced attribute rename. We rolled to prod at 07:50Z. Working on a compatibility shim to map old attribute to new claim during token generation.
2026-03-10T11:10 - Support (Evelyn Chen): Notified #internal-support and #identity Slack channels; requested manual remediation list for critical service accounts used by CI and oncall.

2026-03-11T02:18 - Ravi Singh: Rolled back scim-provisioner to image 2026-03-09-rc. Rolled back reduced new failures but affected accounts still showing null device_trust_status in Okta. Need re-provision step.

2026-03-12T07:30 - Identity (Asha Patel): Ran one-off re-sync job (okta delta reapply) for 42 affected okta IDs; confirmed device_trust_status repopulated. Drafting postmortem and follow-up test plan.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: rolled scim-provisioner to previous image to stop introducing new null attributes. Performed targeted delta re-sync for affected Okta IDs and manually re-mapped 6 critical service accounts to their roles. Permanent fix: compatibility shim merged (PR #4233) to map legacy 'device_trust' to 'device_trust_status' during provisioning; will deploy with canary and integration tests for attribute migrations. Follow-ups: add unit test for attribute rename, update runbook for SCIM schema changes, notify teams to reissue long-lived tokens if they observe 401s.
next_steps: Deploy compatibility shim (PR #4233) to canary region and validate with end-to-end token-exchange smoke tests
Add automated detection and alerting for SCIM attribute drift to SRE monitoring
Run full reconciliation job for Okta org to ensure no remaining null device_trust_status attributes
Update identity runbook to require backward-compatible mapping for any SCIM attribute rename
